articles.headline: India reports 5.83 percent decline in August coal imports driven by higher production.
articles.title: India’s coal imports decline 5.83% in August
articles.summary: Government data shows that India imported 104.57 million tonnes of coal in August, marking a 5.83 percent decrease from the previous year due to rising domestic output and reduced overseas shipments. The power sector saw a significant drop in blending imports, while coking coal shipments for the steel industry also declined as the Union Coal Ministry emphasized strengthening domestic supply chains.
articles.description: According to a statement from the Coal Ministry, the decline was primarily led by the power sector whose imports during the reported period declined 6.4% overall.

articles.headline: Yamaha withdraws MotoGP team from upcoming Qatar race
articles.title: Yamaha pulls out of Qatar MotoGP over ‘situation in the Middle East’
articles.summary: Japanese manufacturer Yamaha pulled its team from next weekend's Qatar Grand Prix on Sunday, citing ongoing company travel restrictions regarding the Middle East. The MotoGP Group expressed disappointment over the absence, noting that safety assurances had been provided. The remainder of the racing grid confirmed their participation for the event at Lusail International Circuit.
articles.description: MotoGP says Yamaha's lack of participation at next weekend's event in Lusail 'carries sporting implications'.

articles.headline: J.P. Nadda criticises opposition rally and defends democratic governance
articles.title: Nadda terms INDIA bloc rally against CEC a ‘foolish and designed drama’
articles.summary: Union Minister J.P. Nadda condemned the opposition INDIA bloc protest in New Delhi as a designed drama meant to subvert democracy. Speaking to reporters on November 1, 2026, the senior Bharatiya Janata Party leader alleged that Congress leader Rahul Gandhi organised the event to provoke public disorder and exploit historical grievances, asserting that India operates strictly through constitutional mandates.
articles.description: Health Minister says Rahul Gandhi was ‘rubbing salt into the wounds of the Sikhs’ on the anniversary of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots

articles.headline: Vizhinjam International Seaport receives its first import container
articles.title: First import container arrives at Vizhinjam
articles.summary: The vessel MSC Sabrina III arrived at the Vizhinjam International Seaport carrying the facility's first import consignment since full-scale export-import operations began in August. The container of engineered building boards from Ningbo, China, was booked by BP2G Logistics and Ship Chandlers for M/s Alteir Group, enabling direct unloading and clearance to reduce transportation costs and delivery times for local entrepreneurs.

articles.headline: Brazil summons Argentina diplomat following Flavio Bolsonaro departure to United States
articles.title: Brazil summons Argentinian diplomat over Bolsonaro’s flight to US
articles.summary: Brazilian authorities summoned charge d'affaires Maria Emilia Cortes to address right-wing politician Flavio Bolsonaro fleeing the country after losing Sunday's presidential election. Bolsonaro faces money-laundering allegations involving Banco Master. He travelled through Argentina to Miami, declaring himself president-elect. The incident strains ties between President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Argentina's libertarian leader Javier Milei, who supported the departure.
articles.description: The move threatens to further strain relations between Brazilian President Lula and his Argentinian counterpart, Milei.

articles.headline: Amit Shah praises Chandigarh Police on its raising day
articles.title: Amit Shah lauds Chandigarh Police, says it set benchmarks for police forces across country
articles.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah lauded the Chandigarh Police on its sixtieth raising day, presenting the force with the President's Colour on November 1, 2026. Shah commended its six decades of service and announced the addition of one hundred forty-one new vehicles to enhance emergency response times, modern policing, and mobility across the northern region.
articles.description: Amit Shah was addressing a gathering on the occasion of the 60th Raising Day event of Chandigarh Police and presenting the President’s Colour to the force

articles.headline: Bulgarian voters cast ballots in presidential run-off amid Black Sea security tensions.
articles.title: Bulgarians vote in presidential run-off amid Black Sea tensions
articles.summary: Citizens are voting in a presidential run-off featuring incumbent Iliana Iotova and former caretaker Prime Minister Andrey Gyurov amid regional security threats. The election follows recent drone attacks on merchant ships off the Black Sea coast. Exit polls will follow the closure of voting at 8pm, with final results anticipated on Monday as candidates address the maritime crisis.
articles.description: Voters in Bulgaria weigh economic challenges and attacks on ships in a race marked by record low turnout.

articles.headline: Is China’s ‘dark tourism’ turning disaster education into entertainment?
articles.title: Is China’s ‘dark tourism’ turning disaster education into entertainment?
articles.description: China is seeing growing interest in ‘dark tourism’, where visitors flock to attractions that recreate natural disasters.

articles.headline: G20 family photo cancelled following European diplomatic boycott over Russia
articles.title: G20 'family photo' cancelled after protests over presence of Russian minister
articles.summary: Organisers cancelled the scheduled family photograph at the Group of Twenty foreign ministers meeting in Atlanta after European diplomats refused to stand alongside Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov. United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio hosted the gathering. British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband participated in the boycott, citing longstanding policies against direct engagement with Russian officials since the invasion of Ukraine.
articles.description: UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband confronted his Russian counterpart at the meeting and accused his government of killing innocent civilians in Ukraine.

articles.headline: Yemeni forces seize military positions in al-Jawf
articles.title: Yemeni government forces seize strategic positions in al-Jawf
articles.summary: Yemen’s internationally recognised government reported that its forces recaptured military positions and strategic heights east of al-Hazm in al-Jawf governorate. The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs stated that more than 290,000 people have fled their homes since fighting escalated in August, while the ongoing siege of Taiz continues to severely restrict deliveries of essential food, fuel and medical supplies.
articles.description: Weapons and ammunition depots are seized after a counteroffensive.

articles.headline: Serbia changes government following years of protests
articles.title: From railway tragedy to gov’t change: Serbia’s two-year fight for justice
articles.summary: Serbia experienced a political shift after the Student List opposition movement won the October general election, following months of protests sparked by the collapse of a railway station canopy in Novi Sad that killed 16 people. Longtime leader Aleksandar Vucic resigned as president and pardoned prosecuted activists before his party conceded defeat in the election.
articles.description: A timeline of events since the deadly train station collapse in Novi Sad, which led to a change of government in Serbia.

articles.headline: Marc Marquez wins Malaysian Grand Prix in Sepang
articles.title: Marquez wins Malaysian Grand Prix to close in on retaining championship
articles.summary: MotoGP champion Marc Marquez won the Malaysian Grand Prix at the Sepang International Circuit, extending his championship lead to 44 points over absent rival Jorge Martin. KTM rider Pedro Acosta finished second and Gresini rider Alex Marquez took third place. The Ducati rider can secure his eighth title at the upcoming Qatar Grand Prix.
articles.description: Marc Marquez takes 44-point lead over Jorge Martin and can seal the MotoGP title in Qatar next weekend.

articles.headline: Israeli protesters urge Jewish-Arab coalition government
articles.title: Israeli protesters urge Jewish-Arab coalition government
articles.description: Israeli protesters urge Jewish-Arab coalition government

articles.headline: Four workers die in Ujjain hotel waste chamber
articles.title: Four die of suspected suffocation while cleaning waste chamber in Madhya Pradesh’s Ujjain hotel
articles.summary: Four workers died from suspected poisonous gas and suffocation after entering a food-waste tank at the Shri Ganga Hotel along the Ujjain-Dewas road in Madhya Pradesh. Ujjain Collector Roshan Kumar Singh and Superintendent of Police Pradeep Sharma confirmed that police and hotel staff recovered the bodies by breaking open the chamber following the incident.
articles.description: Two workers collapsed after entering the food-waste tank at Shri Ganga Hotel on the Ujjain-Dewas road; two more entered to rescue them, and all four died

articles.headline: Malawi cattle farmers travel farther for scarce river fodder
articles.title: Malawi cattle farmers travel farther as El Nino worsens drought
articles.summary: Malawi cattle farmers are travelling longer distances to find river grass as prolonged dry spells and El Nino impact southern Africa. In Mulanje, herders and fodder gatherers struggle with depleted vegetation, higher costs for maize bran, and competition from riverbank agriculture. Cooperatives report declining milk production and squeezed earnings as they await upcoming rains to restore pasture.
articles.description: For many families, keeping cattle alive is becoming an increasingly costly struggle.

articles.headline: Binance freezes half of funds stolen in record cyber attack
articles.title: Crypto giant Binance attempting to recover $6.3bn stolen in hack linked to North Korea
articles.summary: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance has frozen roughly half of the six point three billion dollars stolen in a recent cyber heist. Co-chief executive officer Richard Teng stated the attack involved a self-destruct mechanism and multiple points of breach. Analytics firms and the United States Secret Service are working to trace the funds, while experts warn customers that promises to cover losses may not be legally binding.
articles.description: The cyber-attack, which the company describes as complex, is believed to be the largest ever of its kind.

articles.headline: Record spending drives competitive United States midterm Senate races
articles.title: Where are the most expensive midterm races and who is funding them?
articles.summary: Voters across the United States are preparing for the midterm elections on Tuesday, with control of Congress hinging on expensive Senate races in states like Texas, Ohio, and Michigan. Billionaire donors and political action committees have poured billions into the contests. Republicans have raised more overall, though polls suggest Democrats are favoured to control both chambers.
articles.description: Senate races in Texas, Michigan and Ohio rank among the most expensive in this year's midterm cycle.

articles.headline: Prominent Russian independent news outlet Novaya Gazeta announces its permanent shutdown.
articles.title: They strangled us, says founder of Russian newspaper shut under pressure from authorities
articles.summary: Novaya Gazeta, one of Russia's most high-profile independent news outlets, is shutting down after receiving an eviction order and having its reader donation system disabled by authorities. In a statement, the newspaper accused Russian special services and the repressive state apparatus of forcing it to stop operations. The closure marks the end of an era for fearless investigative journalism under increasing authoritarian pressure.
articles.description: Novaya Gazeta has been one of the most high-profile independent news outlets in Russia over the last three decades.

articles.headline: US appeals court rejects Trump bid to discard California ballots
articles.title: US appeals court again rejects Trump bid to set aside California ballots
articles.summary: An appeals court in the United States has rejected a petition from the administration of President Donald Trump to set aside 20,000 ballots in California over concerns about non-citizen voting. The ruling arrived on Friday, with less than four days until the November 3 midterm elections. Judges Mark Bennett and Gabriel Sanchez formed the majority, ruling the request violated the US Constitution.
articles.description: The 9th Circuit Court calls the petition to remove 20,000 ballots from California's vote count unconstitutional.

articles.headline: G20 drops group photo as Europeans refuse to stand with Lavrov
articles.title: G20 drops group photo as Europeans refuse to stand with Lavrov
articles.summary: The United States scrapped a traditional group photo of foreign ministers after European officials refused to be pictured alongside Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov in Atlanta. The move exposes deep rifts within the Group of 20, whose foreign ministers are meeting for talks overshadowed by ongoing conflicts in Ukraine and Iran. Russian state media reported that Lavrov arrived ahead of the discussions.
articles.description: Sanctioned Russian FM attends Atlanta talks as Iran war, Hormuz disruption and Ukraine divide G20 members.

articles.headline: US tech stocks fall sharply amid mounting concerns over artificial intelligence costs
articles.title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn
articles.summary: United States technology stocks dropped on Friday as financial markets reacted to escalating expenditures associated with artificial intelligence development. Major firms including Intel, Amazon, Alphabet, Reddit, and Roblox experienced notable share price declines following disappointing quarterly earnings reports and warnings about slowing sector growth and search revenue impacts, according to market analysts.
articles.description: Shares in Intel continue to fall while the tech-heavy Nasdaq opens at its lowest level in more than two months.

articles.headline: Supreme Court rules failed relationships cannot transform consensual sex into rape
articles.title: Failed relationships cannot turn consensual sex into rape: Supreme Court
articles.summary: The Supreme Court of India ruled on October 30, 2026, that women cannot retrospectively classify past consensual sexual acts as rape simply because a relationship has ended. Justice B.V. Nagarathna cautioned against the misuse of criminal laws in failed relationships from Kerala, emphasizing that genuine sexual assault cases must be vigorously pursued while preventing the justice system from becoming a tool of vengeance.
articles.description: Court distinguishes between consent allegedly obtained through deception and regret over consensual intimacy after a relationship ends

articles.headline: OpenAI, Google, Microsoft and Anthropic back new scraping opt-out
articles.title: The biggest names in AI are backing a new way to opt out of scraping
articles.summary: OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and Anthropic announced they will adopt a new standard allowing publishers to opt out of web scraping by artificial intelligence companies. Proposed by Kevin Kelley at the Internet Engineering Task Force, the shared policy token will live within a website's robots.txt file. Anthropic has already adopted the signal, while Google and Microsoft plan to support it next year.
articles.description: OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and Anthropic say they will adopt a new standard that publishers can use to opt out of being scraped by AI, as reported earlier by Search Engine Roundtable. With this control, publishers can apply their AI training preferences across multiple AI companies, instead of setting them individually. The shared "policy token" signal […]

articles.headline: Rubio hosts G20 talks as Russia’s Lavrov presence sparks tensions
articles.title: Rubio hosts G20 talks as Russia’s Lavrov presence sparks tensions
articles.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio urged G20 officials to work together to confront threats to the economic order.

articles.headline: Bangladesh forms new wage board to address garment worker protests
articles.title: Bangladesh forms wage board as garment workers protest
articles.summary: Authorities in Bangladesh established a six-member committee to determine a revised minimum wage following demonstrations that disrupted industrial hubs around Dhaka. Demonstrators demanded thirty thousand taka per month, citing soaring living costs. Meanwhile, Ministry of Labour and Employment adviser M Sakhawat Hossain Chowdhury urged employees to resume work as clashes with police injured several people near the capital.
articles.description: Demonstrations held in industrial cities as workers demand wage increase as cost of living rises.

articles.headline: Israeli protesters urge opposition to form coalition with Arab parties
articles.title: Israeli protesters demand opposition ally with Arab parties to oust Netanyahu
articles.summary: Hundreds of demonstrators gathered in Tel Aviv and Jerusalem to demand that Israeli opposition leaders ally with Arab-majority parties to remove Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu from power following an inconclusive election. The proposed coalition could secure sixty-seven seats in parliament, although key opposition figures remain divided over accepting support from Arab factions amid ongoing regional security tensions and political disputes.
articles.description: Arab-majority parties made major gains in elections, fuelled by anger over rhetoric targeting the community from Mr. Netanyahu’s hard-right government, but opposition chief Gadi Eisenkot has not decided whether to seek a coalition with them

articles.headline: European Union and Canada launch Alliance for the Future
articles.title: EU and Canada seek deeper ties amid worsening global uncertainty
articles.summary: The European Union and Canada launched an Alliance for the Future in Montreal, where Prime Minister Mark Carney hosted European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and European Council President Antonio Costa. The two sides signed a digital trade deal and announced measures to increase affordability and secure sovereignty. Carney also announced Canada's participation in a support loan for Kyiv.
articles.description: Both sides signed a digital trade deal, as Trump's trade threats push Washington's allies to seek closer ties elsewhere.

articles.headline: Supreme Court clears income tax assessments for former chief justice sons
articles.title: Supreme Court paves way for IT assessments of two businessmen sons of former CJI Y.K. Sabharwal
articles.summary: The Supreme Court dismissed four appeals filed by Chetan and Nitin Sabharwal, allowing income tax reassessment notices issued for assessment years 2008-09 and 2009-10. A bench comprising Justices J.B. Pardiwala and K. Vinod Chandran upheld that the tax department possessed valid reasons to investigate share transactions utilized to acquire a prime property on Delhi's Sikandra Road in 2010.
articles.description: A Bench of Justices J.B. Pardiwala and K. Vinod Chandran dismissed four appeals filed by Chetan and Nitin Sabharwal, while upholding income tax reassessment notices issued for assessment years 2008-09 and 2009-10

articles.headline: Serbia’s canopy collapse, two years on in a changed country
articles.title: Serbia’s canopy collapse, two years on in a changed country
articles.description: Two years after Novi Sad’s railway station canopy collapse, Serbia marks the second anniversary of the tragedy.

articles.headline: Donald Trump states Flavio Bolsonaro can remain in United States
articles.title: Donald Trump says Flavio Bolsonaro can stay in U.S. as long as he wants amid Brazilian probes
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump announced that defeated Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro may remain in the country indefinitely. Speaking in Florida during a Halloween event, Trump criticized Brazil's recent election. Bolsonaro arrived under humanitarian parole following money laundering probes and the revocation of his passport, while U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio engaged with Brazilian diplomats.
articles.description: Flavio Bolsonaro’s decision to go to the U.S. followed a ruling by a Brazilian Supreme Court Justice to revoke his passport shortly after his loss, as the candidate faces a pair of federal money-laundering probes in Brazil and police there considered him a flight risk

articles.headline: Punjab activists demand justice following the murder of Parvinder Singh Jhota
articles.title: In Punjab, the highway to 2027
articles.summary: Protesters in Mansa town maintain a permanent sit-in camp on October 13 following the fatal shooting of anti-drug crusader Parvinder Singh Jhota. The forty-year-old activist was killed in broad daylight, leaving his last rites delayed by a fortnight as demonstrators demand action against the drug menace that has plagued the northern Indian state for over twenty years.
articles.description: The drug menace in Punjab has stayed at the centre of political and social attention over the past decade or more. With the killing of anti-drug crusader Parvinder Singh Jhota, public emotions are running high. Political parties are hoping to capitalise on this, with the Assembly election due in early 2027, finds Vikas Vasudeva

articles.headline: India marks 79 years of independence following map changes
articles.title: How were the States formed and how has the Indian map changed since 1947?
articles.summary: Following the Indian Independence Act of 1947 and the lapse of British paramountcy, India divided into two independent dominions and integrated numerous princely states. As India marks 79 years of independence, the country now contains 28 states and eight Union Territories after decades of internal boundary reorganisations driven by multiple factors.
articles.description: The last transformation of the Indian map happened in 2019 with the creation of the Union Territories of J&K and Ladakh

articles.headline: Supreme Court directs Election Commission to submit report on Form 7 misuse
articles.title: Supreme Court seeks report from ECI on Form 7 misuse allegations
articles.summary: The Supreme Court of India directed the Election Commission of India to investigate allegations regarding the fraudulent bulk filing of Form 7 applications for voter deletions during the Uttar Pradesh Special Intensive Revision. While responding to a petition filed by Congress Member of Parliament Tanuj Punia, the electoral body stated that although false forms were discovered, none of them were accepted. The bench ordered authorities to file a compliance report.
articles.description: Election Commission says it did not accept any Form 7s filed in violation of norms in U.P.; poll officials took prompt corrective steps, it says after Congress MP alleges widespread fraud during SIR

articles.headline: Portuguese police disperse housing protesters from Lisbon camp
articles.title: Police storm Portugal housing protest camp
articles.summary: Law enforcement officers equipped with shields and batons cleared a tent encampment in Lisbon following a large demonstration against controversial rental legislation. Dozens of police officers moved into Rossio Square to dismantle over fifty tents after issuing warnings regarding illegal encampments. The intervention follows similar police actions that previously sparked criticism and injuries amidst Portugal severe national housing affordability crisis.
articles.description: Dozens of officers, some accompanied by police dogs, moved into Rossio Square in Lisbon early on Sunday.

articles.headline: Two newly elected Bihar independent MLCs extend support to ruling BJP
articles.title: Two newly-elected Bihar Independent MLCs now support BJP
articles.summary: Rahul Raj and Banshidhar Brajwasi extended their support to the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party after winning legislative council elections as independent candidates from Saran Teachers and Tirhut Graduate constituencies. Both individuals previously defeated Janata Dal United candidates. The Bihar BJP formally welcomed the new legislators during a party meeting attended by senior state leaders.
articles.description: Both the Independent candidates, significantly, had defeated the ruling alliance partner Janata Dal-United candidates from their respective constituencies

articles.headline: Depression over Bay of Bengal intensifies into deep depression
articles.title: Depression intensifies into deep depression over Bay of Bengal
articles.summary: A weather system over the southeast Bay of Bengal developed into a deep depression by the early hours of November 1, 2026, according to the India Meteorological Department. Positioned hundreds of kilometres from various coastal cities, the system is projected to evolve into a cyclonic storm over the next six hours and a severe storm by November 2.
articles.description: The system is likely to further intensify into a severe cyclonic storm over the westcentral Bay of Bengal on November 2

articles.headline: US Secretary of State denies helping Flavio Bolsonaro flee Brazil
articles.title: Rubio says Trump administration did not help Bolsonaro flee Brazil to US
articles.summary: United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated on Saturday in Atlanta that the administration did not assist defeated Brazilian politician Flavio Bolsonaro in fleeing to the United States. Bolsonaro, who faces corruption investigations in Brazil, arrived in Miami on Wednesday after receiving a visa following his October 25 election loss to President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva.
articles.description: Trump says defeated presidential candidate, who faces investigation in Brazil, can stay in the US 'as long as he wants'.

articles.headline: Google tests first space-based AI server response in orbit
articles.title: Google’s satellite AI server transmits its first response to Earth
articles.summary: Google has successfully generated its first response from space using an artificial intelligence chip-equipped satellite. The on-board Gemma four model created a haiku after mission operators booted up its tensor processing units earlier this month during Project Suncatcher. Engineers plan to evaluate how the hardware performs under thermal stress and radiation exposure before attempting to launch twin interconnected satellites in 2027.
articles.description: Google's AI chip-equipped satellite has generated its first response from space. In a blog post on Friday, Google says it successfully booted up the satellite's Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), allowing the on-board Gemma 4 model to follow through on a prompt to create a haiku about being in space: Blue marble below Data streams in […]

articles.headline: Canelo Alvarez defeats Christian Mbilli to reclaim WBC super middleweight title
articles.title: Canelo Alvarez defeats Christian Mbilli to reclaim WBC title in Riyadh
articles.summary: Saul Canelo Alvarez secured a 12-round decision victory over French fighter Christian Mbilli in Riyadh on Sunday to recapture his World Boxing Council super middleweight title. The 36-year-old Mexican boxer triumphed in Saudi Arabia despite regional security concerns, earning judges' scores of 115-112, 116-111, and 117-110 to add another belt to his storied professional career.
articles.description: Mexican boxing star wins 12-round decision to defeat the French fighter and regain the super middleweight belt.

articles.headline: Golden State Valkyries defeat Atlanta Dream to capture first WNBA crown
articles.title: Golden State Valkyries defeat Atlanta Dream to capture first WNBA crown
articles.summary: Gabby Williams scored 30 points, including 28 in the second half, to lead the Golden State Valkyries to a 68-63 victory over the Atlanta Dream on Saturday in San Francisco. The win in game seven secured the Women's National Basketball Association championship in the franchise's second season, with Williams earning the Finals Most Valuable Player award.
articles.description: Gabby Williams, named Most Valuable Player, sets records for most points (137) and most steals (18) in the WNBA Finals.

articles.headline: James Talarico challenges Republicans in costly Texas Senate race
articles.title: Democrats are used to heartbreak in Texas - could Talarico turn the tide?
articles.summary: Democratic candidate James Talarico is challenging Republicans in a high-stakes United States Senate race in Texas that has exceeded half a billion dollars in spending. Recent polls indicate a tight contest in the reliably red state, prompting visits from political figures including President Donald Trump. Strategists warn that a potential Democratic victory could significantly alter the political landscape both locally and nationally.
articles.description: The state's $500m Senate race may be the most closely watched in the US midterms, and is about far more than control of Congress.

articles.headline: Vatican confirms Pope Leo XIV cast mail-in ballot in US
articles.title: How can Pope Leo vote in U.S. elections while serving as the sovereign of Vatican City? | Explained
articles.summary: The Holy See Press Office confirmed that Chicago-born Pope Leo XIV, formerly known as Robert Francis Prevost, has cast his vote in the United States midterm elections. The Vatican stated that the pontiff has exercised his right to vote as a United States citizen whenever eligible by submitting his mail-in ballot in Chicago, maintaining a long-standing practice of civic participation.
articles.description: Does becoming the Pope automatically mean giving up American citizenship? Can a foreign head of state retain the right to vote in U.S. elections? How does Pope Leo XIV’s dual status as the sovereign of Vatican City and a US citizen affect his voting rights?

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh urban local body elections begin under tight security
articles.title: Urban local body elections begin in Andhra Pradesh
articles.summary: Voting for mayors, chairpersons, and ward members across 13 municipal corporations and 79 municipalities and Nagar Panchayats in Andhra Pradesh began at 7:00 am on November 1, 2026. State Election Commissioner Anil Chandra Punetha is monitoring the process amid heavy security deployment, including closed-circuit television cameras and drones, following earlier violence during the nomination filing phase across thousands of sensitive polling stations.
articles.description: State Election Commissioner Anil Chandra Punetha and his team of officers are personally monitoring the conduct of the elections, for which elaborate arrangements were made, including the installation of CCTV cameras and deployment of drones at places where clashes are anticipated

articles.headline: India records below average monsoon despite shaping El Nino
articles.title: Why even a strong El Niño does not guarantee a poor Indian monsoon
articles.summary: The 2026 southwest monsoon concluded nearly thirteen percent below the long term average of eighty seven centimeters, accompanied by a developing El Nino expected to peak in December. East and Northeast India experienced their driest season since records began in 1901. Historically, strong El Nino events do not always guarantee poor monsoon outcomes.
articles.description: Seven Indian monsoons since 1950 have run into a moderate or strong El Niño. Of these, in five years, including 2026, monsoon rainfall levels were at least 10% lower than the long-term average. The IMD refers to this level as 'deficient’. The 2023 season was something of an exception with ‘below average’ rainfall. However, 1997 had ‘average’ rainfall

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu cabinet approves Social Justice Survey
articles.title: How significant is the TVK-led regime’s move to hold Social Justice Survey? | Explained
articles.summary: The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam-led regime in Tamil Nadu has officially approved the formation of a multi-member panel to conduct a Social Justice Survey. Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay announced the decision during a cabinet meeting in Chennai on October 29, 2026, fulfilling an earlier commitment made by Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar regarding state demographic data collection.
articles.description: The feature of an ‘open column’, where respondents can state their caste during the second phase of the Census, to be carried out in most parts of the country during February next year, has forced many parties and other stakeholders to express concerns over the utility of the whole exercise

articles.headline: Vehicles torched in Pulivendula hours before municipal elections begin
articles.title: Vehicles torched ahead of polls in Pulivendula
articles.summary: Several vehicles were set on fire in Pulivendula hours before municipal elections commenced on Saturday morning. Police reported that three cars, ten motorcycles, and a tractor were destroyed near Madhusudhan Reddy's orchard. Polling subsequently opened briskly amidst brief clashes and stone pelting between rival cadres, prompting law enforcement intervention across multiple wards in the town.
articles.description: The incident happened around midnight near the orchard belonging to Madhusudhan Reddy, where three cars, ten motorcycles and a tractor were fully burnt

articles.headline: Maharashtra FDA issues strict order to curb expired food sales
articles.title: Maharashtra FDA issues order to curb sale, repackaging of expired food items
articles.summary: The Food and Drug Administration has introduced a mandatory requirement for companies to provide proof of proper disposal and destruction certificates from approved facilities. According to FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe, recent state operations led to two registered cases and the seizure of adulterated goods worth five crore rupees. Authorities also cracked down on illegal activities in Bhiwandi and other regions.
articles.description: Speaking at a press conference in October 30, Mr. Mundhe says that instead of destroying stale and expired food items properly, they are being “disposed of only on paper.” These goods are brought back after being repacked by some agents and then sold to citizens. In some cases, even the production dates are being manipulated

articles.headline: Prime minister Modi highlights historic poverty decline citing World Bank report
articles.title: PM Modi cites World Bank report to highlight ‘historic’ fall in India’s extreme poverty
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi highlighted a World Bank report showing that India recorded one of the world's fastest poverty reductions, with 49.6 crore people moving out of poverty between 2011 and 2023. According to the October 2026 brief, extreme poverty plummeted from 27.1 percent to 2.6 percent, while employment grew by 13.4 crore in six years. Modi contrasted his administration's targeted efforts with past opposition campaigns during the announcement on Instagram.
articles.description: In a post on Instagram featuring the inspiring and energetic song ‘Thaan Liya’ from the Bollywood movie ‘Dasvi’ as background music, Mr. Modi highlighted that the “historic" drop in poverty represents a generational surge in opportunities

articles.headline: INDIA bloc stages Chalo Dilli march to demand election commissioner resignation
articles.title: INDIA bloc rally today: What to know about the Ramlila Maidan protest
articles.summary: The Indian National Developmental Inclusive Alliance is staging the Chalo Dilli protest march in New Delhi on November first to demand Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over alleged electoral roll irregularities. Concurrently, the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party organised counter demonstrations. Delhi traffic police implemented strict diversions while thousands of security personnel monitored the demonstrations.
articles.description: Here’s what to know about the INDIA bloc mega rally in New Delhi, demanding the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar.

articles.headline: Marble dump yard in Rajasthan attracts tourists while endangering villagers
articles.title: ‘Like Kashmir’: How a toxic marble dump yard became a tourist spot in India
articles.summary: A 300-acre marble slurry dumping site in Kishangarh has become a popular tourist destination resembling a snow-clad landscape in India's Rajasthan state. However, approximately 5,000 residents living in nearby villages suffer from severe health complications, including respiratory illnesses, skin allergies, and dental issues. According to studies and local testimonies, toxic dust contaminates soil, ruins crops, and pollutes groundwater supplies.
articles.description: Vast 'snow yard' in otherwise arid Rajasthan attracts hundreds of tourists daily, but residents face major health risks.

articles.headline: Indian regulators order Sun Pharma to halt eye-care drug production
articles.title: India orders Sun Pharma to halt eye-care drug production at plant after quality lapses
articles.summary: Indian drug regulatory authorities ordered Sun Pharmaceutical Industries to suspend the manufacturing and distribution of ophthalmic products at its Assam facility following quality management lapses identified during a joint inspection. The action follows the company's voluntary recall of multiple batches of eye-care brands. Sun Pharma stated that it has implemented remedial measures and submitted a compliance report currently under review by regulators.
articles.description: India’s drug quality standards have come under increased scrutiny at home and overseas in recent years after locally made cough syrups were linked to ‌the deaths of children in India and also in countries including Gambia and Uzbekistan

articles.headline: United Nations demands independent investigation into staffer death in Houthi custody
articles.title: UN demands investigation after staffer’s death in Houthi custody in Yemen
articles.summary: The United Nations has called for an urgent and transparent investigation into the death of Mohammad el-Shami, an employee of the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights who died in Houthi detention in Yemen. Detained since June 2024 alongside over 60 other aid workers on unproven espionage allegations, el-Shami is the second UN staff member to die in custody. UN High Commissioner Volker Turk and Secretary-General Antonio Guterres demanded answers and the immediate release of remaining detainees.
articles.description: Mohammad el-Shami had been held since June 2024, when he and many other UN and NGO workers were accused of being spies.

articles.headline: France protests enter third week as police fire tear gas
articles.title: France protests enter third week as police fire tear gas
articles.description: Police used tear gas to disperse protesters as demonstrations entered a third week ahead in France.

articles.headline: Bolivia declares nationwide state of emergency due to El Nino
articles.title: Bolivia declares state of emergency over El Nino weather pattern
articles.summary: Bolivian President Rodrigo Paz signed a decree establishing a nationwide state of emergency to deploy rescue teams against floods and drought. According to government reports, drought affects 78,000 families across six departments and has killed over 75,000 cattle. Globally, scientists predict the climate phenomenon could cause more than 450,000 deaths.
articles.description: Drought is affecting 78,000 families and has led to loss of over 75,000 cattle, as El Nino due to peak in late 2026.

articles.headline: Evacuees from Oleshky reunite with family during ceasefire
articles.title: Ukrainian evacuees from Russian-occupied Oleshky reunite with family
articles.summary: Exhausted residents from the Russian-occupied Ukrainian town of Oleshky crossed into Ukraine during a six-day humanitarian ceasefire mediated by United States First Lady Melania Trump and Pope Leo XIV. Evacuees who faced severe food shortages and starvation reunited with family at the border, while officials delivered medical aid and supplies.
articles.description: Starved and exhausted residents of Oleshky arrive in Ukraine after months of isolation, but some stay behind.

articles.headline: India’s largest dam planned to counter China faces Indigenous revolt
articles.title: India’s largest dam planned to counter China faces Indigenous revolt
articles.description: Indigenous people of Arunachal Pradesh are protesting a mega dam planned to counter China's upstream hydropower project.

articles.headline: The murder of Javits Frimpong, a bullied schoolboy in The Bronx
articles.title: The murder of Javits Frimpong, a bullied schoolboy in The Bronx
articles.description: Thousands of people have held vigils for a 15-year-old Ghanaian boy who was chased down and killed in New York.

articles.headline: Taiwan deploys ships to monitor Chinese Coast Guard patrol
articles.title: Taiwan says China harassing shipping with east coast patrol
articles.summary: Taiwan deployed its own vessels to monitor two Chinese Coast Guard ships conducting a patrol off Taiwan's east coast. The Taiwanese Coast Guard stated that China was harassing shipping and attempting to exert jurisdiction. Additionally, Taiwan reported that China sent another ship close to the Taiwan-controlled Pratas Islands.
articles.description: Taiwan's Coast Guard said China's "attempts to harass ships at sea through radio ‌communications are a clear expansion of power that violate international law, undermine regional peace and stability, and deviate from reality"

articles.headline: Field trainers prepare enumerators for upcoming population enumeration phase of census
articles.title: Census 2027: What are the new questions, and how are enumerators being trained? | Explained
articles.summary: Field trainers are preparing enumerators in Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Goa and Punjab for the second phase of the census beginning on December 1, 2026. Enumerators will ask forty questions, including thirteen new categories covering details such as caste, religion and Aadhaar numbers, requiring approximately twenty to twenty-five minutes per respondent across blocks of up to eight hundred people.
articles.description: As Uttar Pradesh and three other poll-bound States — Uttarakhand, Goa and Punjab — prepare to launch the second phase of Census 2027 on December 1, field trainers are briefing about 34 lakh enumerators on 40 questions that will require longer, more sensitive interviews and digital data entry, including caste, religion, Aadhaar access and parents’ details

articles.headline: Precious metals post consecutive monthly declines amid rising inflation and rate hike fears
articles.title: Gold, silver lose sheen
articles.summary: Gold and silver recorded negative returns for the second straight month in October due to surging crude oil prices, escalating inflation concerns, and potential United States interest rate increases. Comex gold dropped by 7.26 percent to $3,884.9 per ounce, while Comex silver fell steeply by 19.1 percent to $49.13 per ounce by the end of October, according to data published on November 2.
articles.description: Gold and silver have clocked negative returns. Even the outlook for both gold and silver have turned negative. Precious metal prices are likely to drift lower until resistance level is breached

articles.headline: Indian-origin candidates contest across United States midterm elections
articles.title: Who are the Indian-origin candidates in U.S. midterm elections?
articles.summary: Numerous individuals with South Asian heritage are running for public office in the November 2026 legislative contests across various American states. Prominent incumbent lawmakers and new nominees are seeking positions in Congress, state executive offices, and local governments. These campaigns encompass multiple jurisdictions, highlighting the growing political participation of this community within the American electoral system.
articles.description: Democratic lawmakers Ro Khanna, Pramila Jayapal, Ami Bera and Suhas Subramanyam are seeking re-election to the U.S. Congress

articles.headline: Talarico draws a packed campus rally, but can he win over young voters?
articles.title: Talarico draws a packed campus rally, but can he win over young voters?
articles.description: Al Jazeera’s @EmmaWithrow attended a packed rally for Democrat Senate Candidate James Talarico at Texas A&M.

articles.headline: US judge dismisses Donald Trump defamation lawsuit against media outlet
articles.title: Judge dismisses Trump's lawsuit against Wall Street Journal over Epstein birthday book
articles.summary: A United States judge dismissed President Donald Trump's ten billion dollar lawsuit against The Wall Street Journal and parent company Dow Jones. Judge Darrin Gayles ruled the defamation case violated the First Amendment and lacked proof of actual malice. The suit followed the newspaper's report on a 2003 birthday book letter concerning Jeffrey Epstein, which Trump denied writing.
articles.description: Trump had sued the media outlet after it published a letter to Epstein purportedly written and signed by the president as part of a birthday book.

articles.headline: Polish president holds crisis talks following suspension of top court judge
articles.title: Polish president holds crisis talks in court standoff
articles.summary: Polish President Karol Nawrocki held urgent crisis talks with political leaders after the sudden suspension of Constitutional Tribunal chief judge Bogdan Swieczkowski. Prime Minister Donald Tusk accused nationalist opposition figures of undermining democracy, while the European Commission urged the president to accept new judge nominations to resolve the constitutional standoff.
articles.description: A dispute over the politicisation of Poland's constitutional court is deepening, with no side appearing to back down.

articles.headline: Trump agrees to grant visa for mother of slain Bronx teenager
articles.title: Mamdani says Trump has agreed to grant visa to mother of Ghanian teen killed in Bronx shooting
articles.summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced that President Donald Trump agreed to immediately grant a visa to the mother of Javits Frimpong, a 15-year-old immigrant from Ghana who was shot dead in the Bronx. The teenager was killed on Thursday morning while walking to school, and the shooting remains under active police investigation.
articles.description: The teenager, Javits Frimpong, was on his way to school in a Bronx neighbourhood shortly before 9.30 a.m. October 29 when he was shot in the abdomen, New York City police said

articles.headline: ICE agent’s violent shove propels woman through the air
articles.title: ICE agent’s violent shove propels woman through the air
articles.description: A witness has captured video of an ICE agent violently shoving a teacher who was blocking his car in Chicago.

articles.headline: Parents of deceased IIT student seek judicial probe
articles.title: IIT Bombay student death: Parents seek CBI investigation
articles.summary: The parents of Sahil Wakode, an Indian Institute of Technology Bombay student who died by suicide on September 18, have filed a petition in the Bombay High Court. Ravindra and Sonali Wakode requested an independent investigation by the Central Bureau of Investigation or a Special Investigation Team, alleging that police failed to properly probe caste-based humiliation and remarks faced by their son.
articles.description: The petition alleged that police had failed to probe the case with the seriousness it merits and, hence, sought the probe to be monitored by a retired judge

articles.headline: Brighton defeats Manchester City while Chelsea overcomes Manchester United
articles.title: Brighton stun Manchester City, 10-man Manchester United beaten by Chelsea
articles.summary: Brighton secured a one nil victory against Manchester City in the Premier League to move two points behind the leaders. Yasin Ayari scored the decisive goal in the eleventh minute. Meanwhile, ten man Manchester United suffered a two zero defeat at Chelsea after Lisandro Martinez received two yellow cards and Cole Palmer converted a penalty kick.
articles.description: Third-placed Brighton ended their wait for a first away win against City at the 18th attempt to bolster dreams of challenging for the title

articles.headline: Dutch authorities rescue 38 migrants from drifting boat
articles.title: Dutch authorities rescue 38 people adrift in rubber boat
articles.summary: Military police intercepted 36 Afghan men and two Sudanese suspects aboard a motorless inflatable vessel in the Zeeland province. Officials arrested the two Sudanese nationals for suspected human trafficking. The origin and intended destination of the group remain unknown, marking an unusual maritime interception for the Netherlands compared with frequent crossings elsewhere in Europe.
articles.description: Migrant boats are rarely found in Dutch waters, and authorities are still trying to establish where this one came from.

articles.headline: Palestine Action supporters arrested outside US embassy in London
articles.title: Palestine Action supporters arrested outside US embassy in London
articles.description: Hundreds of protesters gathered outside the US Embassy in London to oppose the UK government's ban on Palestine Action.

articles.headline: South Africa defeats Australia by 176 runs to clinch Test series
articles.title: Harmer the hero as South Africa clinches series win
articles.summary: Off-spinner Simon Harmer claimed career-best figures of six for sixteen as South Africa dismissed Australia for 111 runs on October 31 to win the third Test by 176 runs at Newlands and secure a two-to-one series victory. The thirty-seven-year-old finished with ten wickets in the match, while Kagiso Rabada reached 350 Test wickets, displacing Australia from the top of the rankings.
articles.description: Simon Harmer finished with match figures of 10 for 120, his first 10-wicket haul in Tests; Harmer’s second innings figures read: 21.1-14-16-6

articles.headline: New court filing challenges Trump administration voter list in California
articles.title: Legal filing questions Trump’s claims of non-citizen voting in California
articles.summary: A court submission by the Coalition for Humane Immigrant Rights revealed that over forty percent of names on a voter list sent to California by the United States administration were absent from state rolls. Two data scientists from the University of California, Los Angeles conducted the analysis ahead of the upcoming midterm elections.
articles.description: Data scientists find that many 'likely non-citizens' identified by the Trump administration were erroneously flagged.

articles.title: Fiery confrontations between protestors and police in Albania
articles.description: Fiery confrontations between protestors and police in Albania

articles.headline: Nigerian health authorities investigate two suspected Ebola virus cases
articles.title: Health authorities probe two suspected Ebola cases in northeast Nigeria
articles.summary: Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention officials are investigating two suspected Ebola cases in the northeastern region after isolating both individuals. Laboratory testing and contact tracing are currently underway following the country's first case in over a decade on October 20. The ongoing outbreak involves the Bundibugyo strain originating from the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
articles.description: The two individuals have been isolated while officials carry out contact tracing and laboratory testing.

articles.headline: Madras High Court Advocates Association challenges 1965 Union Cabinet decision on language
articles.title: Madras High Court Advocates Association challenges 1965 Union Cabinet decision to continue English as common language for Supreme Court and all High Courts
articles.summary: The Madras High Court Advocates Association filed a public interest litigation challenging a 1965 Union Cabinet Committee decision mandating English as the common language for the Supreme Court and all High Courts. The association argues the policy violates constitutional equality and freedom provisions, and hinders regional languages like Tamil from becoming official court languages.
articles.description: Says, the 1965 decision came to its notice only in 2025 pursuant to details obtained by a lawyer under the Right to Information Act, 2005

articles.headline: London police arrest 139 people outside United States Embassy for supporting Palestine Action
articles.title: London police arrest 139 people outside U.S. Embassy for supporting banned pro-Palestinian group
articles.summary: London's Metropolitan Police detained 139 demonstrators outside the United States Embassy for supporting the proscribed organisation Palestine Action. The demonstration follows the United Kingdom government's designation of the group as a terrorist organisation last year, which makes support punishable by up to fourteen years in prison ahead of a Supreme Court appeal.
articles.description: Many of those protesting were retirees and were holding signs reading: “I oppose genocide, I support Palestine Action”

articles.headline: District of Columbia and Virginia file lawsuit to block triumphal arch
articles.title: District of Columbia and Virginia sue to block Trump’s triumphal arch plans
articles.summary: Washington, District of Columbia and Virginia filed a joint lawsuit challenging President Donald Trump's plans to construct a seventy-six metre triumphal arch near Arlington National Cemetery. The legal action warns that the three-year project would create severe traffic congestion, pollute the Potomac River, and require congressional authorisation before any ground can be broken.
articles.description: The monument has sparked fierce opposition from local governments fearing disruption to traffic and historic views.

articles.headline: Akhilesh Yadav pitches Gorakhpur versus Varanasi narrative following Legislative Council polls
articles.title: Akhilesh pitches Gorakhpur vs Kashi narrative, eyes inroads among Brahmins, business community
articles.summary: Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav highlighted an alleged disagreement between the Bharatiya Janata Party leadership by contrasting Gorakhpur and Varanasi election results. Addressing party members in Lucknow, he accused the administration of mistreating Brahmins and business communities while claiming broad support from various demographic groups across Uttar Pradesh.
articles.description: Akhilesh Yadav is attempting to make inroads among Brahmins and the Bania community by accusing the Chief Minister and his regime of being anti-Brahmins and Banias

articles.headline: Israel’s allegations of Qatari election interference rejected
articles.title: Israel’s allegations of Qatari election interference rejected
articles.description: Israel’s allegations of Qatari election interference rejected

articles.headline: Ranked-choice voting systems draw attention during United States midterm elections
articles.title: What is ranked-choice voting and how does it work in US elections?
articles.summary: Alaska and Maine utilise statewide ranked-choice voting, allowing citizens to order preferences rather than select a single candidate to eliminate spoiler effects. The method faces ongoing scrutiny, notably in Alaska where two candidates named Dan Sullivan share the ballot and President Donald Trump filed a lawsuit regarding potential voter confusion.
articles.description: Ranked-choice voting in Alaska could shape a key 2026 race, amid a US lawsuit involving two candidates named Dan Sullivan.

articles.headline: Kerala Home Minister calls for strong cybercrime defense shield
articles.title: Keralam needs strong security shield to combat cybercrimes, says Home Minister Chennithala
articles.summary: Speaking at an event organised by the Kerala Police, Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala highlighted the registration of over fifty thousand cyber cases in the state during the past year. He announced plans to establish cyber defence centres in two hundred fifty degree colleges to enhance vigilance and awareness among citizens regarding online financial frauds and smart phone safety.
articles.description: Plans are afoot to begin cyber defence centres in 250 degree colleges in the State to step up vigilance against cybercrimes

articles.headline: Cochin Cancer Research Centre will become treatment excellence institution
articles.title: Cochin Cancer Research Centre ​will be ​developed into centre of ​excellence​, says Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan
articles.summary: Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan announced government support to develop the regional facility into a premier medical and research establishment during its tenth anniversary celebration. He emphasised the necessity of affordable public healthcare options, disease prevention, and early diagnosis to prevent families from facing severe financial distress due to high medical expenses.
articles.description: A comprehensive development plan for the next five years will be prepared and implemented in phases, says CM

articles.headline: Manoj Sinha marks Jammu and Kashmir foundation day highlighting security gains
articles.title: We did not buy peace; we established peace in J&K: L-G Manoj Sinha on UT Foundation Day
articles.summary: Jammu and Kashmir Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha stated during the eighth Union Territory Foundation Day that the abrogation of Article 370 ended fear and established peace. Speaking on October 31, 2026, he highlighted the elimination of over 780 terrorists and actions against narcotics. The event was attended by officials including Chief Secretary Atal Dulloo, though regional ruling party leaders were absent.
articles.description: L-G Manoj Sinha said terror, separatism and stone-pelting have given way to democracy, development and public participation after Article 370 was removed

articles.headline: IIM Bangalore achieves full summer placement with median stipend at two lakh rupees
articles.title: IIM-Bangalore records 100% summer placements, with median stipend at ₹2 lakh per month
articles.summary: Indian Institute of Management Bangalore concluded its summer placement process for the 2026-28 cohort on October 29, 2026, with all 608 students receiving offers from 128 organisations. According to a release from the institution, consulting comprised over half of all recruitments, while first-time recruiters accounted for approximately 40% of participating companies during the placement week.
articles.description: Consulting accounts for 50.7% of offers; first-time recruiters account for 40% of participating organisations

articles.headline: Voters question electoral roll name deletions during public impeachment of Gyanesh Kumar
articles.title: At CEC’s ‘public impeachment’, voters question deletion of names from rolls
articles.summary: Opposition alliance leaders held a mock impeachment event on October 31, 2026, in New Delhi against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Citizens and activists testified about alleged unlawful voter roll deletions and citizenship demands during special intensive revision exercises. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge moved the motion at the gathering presided over by Meira Kumar.
articles.description: Student leaders and activists also spoke at the event, which was held at Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge’s residence in New Delhi

articles.headline: Hackers target Binance in largest cryptocurrency heist with billions stolen
articles.title: How vulnerable are cryptocurrency platforms?
articles.summary: Hackers targeted Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, stealing approximately 6.3 billion dollars in client assets in what is described as the largest crypto heist in history. Analysts suspect North Korean state-backed hackers carried out the attack, prompting critics to demand stricter regulations to restore investor confidence in digital platforms.
articles.description: Hackers have targeted Binance, the world’s largest exchange.

articles.headline: Marco Rubio clarifies United States had no direct involvement in Flavio Bolsonaro departure
articles.title: Rubio says U.S. not directly involved in Flavio Bolsonaro’s flight from Brazil
articles.summary: United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated on October 31, 2026, that Washington was not directly involved in Flavio Bolsonaro leaving Brazil following his October 25 election loss. Mr. Bolsonaro arrived in the United States with his family on October 28 after a court ordered his passports seized amidst multiple investigations facing the politician.
articles.description: Bolsonaro, who lost his bid to be president in the October 25 run-off vote, arrived with his family in the U.S. on October 28

articles.headline: London police arrest 139 demonstrators during Palestine Action rally
articles.title: London police arrest 139 as hundreds protest Palestine Action ban
articles.summary: Metropolitan Police detained 139 individuals outside the United States embassy in London after crowds defied warnings and gathered to protest the government proscription of Palestine Action. Demonstrations occurred ahead of a Supreme Court appeal challenging the terror designation, drawing criticism from figures including Labour Party MP John McDonnell regarding freedom of speech and peaceful assembly restrictions.
articles.description: Demonstrations in London and Edinburgh come days before a UK Supreme Court appeal challenging the group's proscription.

articles.headline: Polish expert discusses political crisis following disputed constitutional tribunal posts
articles.title: Polish crisis could help PM Tusk or backfire against him and President Nawrocki in 2027 polls, says expert
articles.summary: Polish President Karol Nawrocki ordered his aircraft to return to Warsaw from Spanish airspace as a political crisis erupted with Prime Minister Donald Tusk over Constitutional Tribunal appointments. Krzysztof Marcin Zalewski, Chairperson of the Boym Institute, discussed the trajectory of this political conflict and its potential implications for the 2027 elections during an interview on October 31, 2026.
articles.description: Polish Expert Krzysztof Marcin Zalewski on the trajectory of the current political crisis and the way ahead for the Donald Tusk government

articles.headline: Evacuees of Russian-occupied Oleshky reunited with families
articles.title: Evacuees of Russian-occupied Oleshky reunited with families
articles.description: Ukrainian residents evacuated from Russian-occupied city of Oleshky have arrived in Ukrainian-controlled territory.

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister MK Stalin demands action against police over professor arrest
articles.title: Take action against officials who arrested MIDS professor, Stalin urges T.N. government
articles.summary: The Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam leader urged authorities to punish officers who exceeded their authority by detaining Madras Institute of Development Studies professor Kalaiarasan over fake social media comments. The politician emphasized that functional administrations should address public criticism through substantive ideas rather than deploying police forces against critical voices.
articles.description: He says creating a society in which there is no room for questions is not a sign of good governance

articles.headline: Centre releases Rs 4,504 crore tax devolution instalment to Karnataka
articles.title: Centre releases ₹4,504-crore additional instalment of tax devolution to Karnataka
articles.summary: The central government disbursed an additional tax devolution instalment totalling over Rs 1.09 lakh crore to state governments, with Karnataka receiving Rs 4,504 crore. According to a Finance Ministry statement, the funds aim to help states accelerate capital spending and finance development and welfare expenditures ahead of the festive season.

articles.headline: Student attacked with electric chainsaw in Raptadu school classroom
articles.title: Class 10 girl attacked with chainsaw in classroom in Anantapur; perpetrator nabbed within hours
articles.summary: A tenth-class student was critically injured after being attacked with an electric chainsaw inside a classroom at Zilla Parishad High School in Raptadu on Saturday. The perpetrator, identified as a close relative named Hemanth, was arrested hours later at Dharmavaram railway station. Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu expressed shock and ordered a thorough investigation as the victim was transferred to Bengaluru for advanced medical treatment.
articles.description: Victim shifted to Bengaluru for better treatment; perpetrator, a close relative of the victim, was arrested at Dharmavaram railway station within hours of the incident

articles.headline: Narendra Modi inaugurates tourism and infrastructure projects in Ekta Nagar
articles.title: Modi says Opposition has become destructive force; calls for unity
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated twenty-three development projects worth 307.83 crore rupees and laid foundation stones for eight others in Ekta Nagar, Gujarat, on October 31, 2026. The initiatives aim to upgrade visitor facilities and civic infrastructure around the Statue of Unity. The program coincided with Rashtriya Ekta Diwas, marking the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.
articles.description: The Prime Minister also laid the foundation stones for eight development projects worth ₹118.88 crore, taking the total outlay for the 31 projects to ₹426.71 crore

articles.headline: Brighton defeats Manchester City to close Premier League gap
articles.title: Brighton shock Man City, closing gap on Premier League leader to two points
articles.summary: Brighton secured a 1-0 victory over Manchester City in the Premier League thanks to an early goal by Yasin Ayari and inspired goalkeeping by Bart Verbruggen. The result moves third-placed Brighton within two points of the leaders, handing manager Fabian Hurzeler's team a historic away win at City.
articles.description: Yasin Ayari goal hands third-placed Brighton 1-0 win at Manchester City, with two points separating top three in EPL.

articles.headline: Uttarakhand mandates co-pilots on Char Dham chartered flights
articles.title: Uttarakhand makes co-pilots mandatory on Char Dham chartered flights after crash killed six
articles.summary: Following a fatal helicopter crash in Joshimath, the Uttarakhand Civil Aviation Development Authority (UCADA) made two-pilot crew configurations mandatory for pilgrimage charter services starting November 2. UCADA Chief Executive Officer Prateek Jain stated that pilots must also submit post-flight weather reports and obtain prior approval for take-offs and landings.
articles.description: The Uttarakhand Civil Aviation Development Authority has also made it compulsory for all pilots to submit a report to the authorities after every flight, detailing weather conditions and other important operational information

articles.headline: Jerusalem Daily: Who will form Israel’s next government?
articles.title: Jerusalem Daily: Who will form Israel’s next government?
articles.description: Netanyahu and Eisenkot are locked in a struggle to form a governing coalition in the Knesset.

articles.headline: State government sanctions special funds for drinking water amid El Nino
articles.title: Govt. sanctions special funds for alternative drinking water sources amid El Nino concerns
articles.summary: The state government approved Rs 120 crore for alternative drinking water arrangements linked to the Singur reservoir and Rs 1 crore each for other districts to counter potential El Nino shortages. Panchayat Raj and Rural Water Supply Minister Danasari Anasuya Seethakka instructed officials to map vulnerable villages, secure local water sources, and expedite groundwater recharge works.

articles.headline: Pakistan defeats Sri Lanka by three wickets in tri-series final
articles.title: Pakistan beat Sri Lanka as Zaman’s century turns thrilling tri-series final
articles.summary: Opener Fakhar Zaman scored 127 runs to lead Pakistan to a three-wicket victory over Sri Lanka in the one-day international tri-series final at Gaddafi Stadium in Lahore. Pakistan successfully chased a target of 325, reaching 331-7 in 48.3 overs with contributions from Arafat Minhas and Saad Baig after Kamindu Mendis had earlier hit an unbeaten century for Sri Lanka.
articles.description: Fakhar Zaman's century outdoes Kamindu Mendis and propels Pakistan to three-wicket win against Sri Lanka in cricket final.

articles.headline: Democratic healthcare professionals surge as candidates in the midterm elections
articles.title: A cure for Trump? Why Democratic doctors are running in the 2026 midterms
articles.summary: Public health workers and physicians across the United States are increasingly running for congressional seats in the midterm elections. Experts attribute this political mobilization partly to voter frustration with rising medical expenses and the healthcare policies promoted by Republican President Donald Trump. Healthcare remains a prominent voting issue, underscored by a Pew Research Center poll showing strong voter concern.
articles.description: Democratic doctors aim to convert the backlash against the Trump administration’s health policies into midterm votes.

articles.headline: Dakar prepares to host the 2026 Youth Olympic Games
articles.title: Dakar Youth Olympics: Who gets to hold the flame?
articles.summary: Senegal is welcoming approximately 2,700 athletes, coaches, and supporters for the 2026 Youth Olympic Games opening in Dakar. International Olympic Committee leader Kirsty Coventry described the event as an opportunity for Africa to demonstrate its capabilities despite the nation facing financial and political challenges. The competitions feature diverse teenage athletes, though geopolitical tensions have already emerged regarding national representations.
articles.description: Senegal makes history by becoming the first African country to host an Olympic event.

articles.headline: Enforcement Directorate arrests four individuals in cross-border drug network probe
articles.title: ED arrests four more accused, including Myanmar national, in cross-border drug network
articles.summary: The Enforcement Directorate took four suspects into custody, including Myanmar national Thangcintuang, as part of an ongoing investigation into an international narco-hawala network. Following raids conducted under Operation Trident across Assam, Mizoram, and Manipur, the agency uncovered extensive financial records detailing currency exchanges and payments made in kind to drug suppliers located in Myanmar.
articles.description: Chintuang was a Myanmar-based supplier of the 49.1 kg methamphetamine consignment seized in August 2025, while Lalrammuana was the main handler and Jabrul Haque its intended receiver at Damchhera-Kanhmun border; Abu Saleh was allegedly the operator whose account received ₹11.44 crore

articles.headline: France deploys 70,000 security personnel as youth protests spread across Europe
articles.title: Clashes break out between police and protesters in Paris
articles.summary: France deployed 70,000 police and gendarmes on October 31, 2026, for a third weekend of protests over living costs and education. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez warned of high disorder risks after dark. Authorities restricted march routes and imposed curfews. Meanwhile, youth demonstrations and TikTok-driven rallies also spread to Germany, Spain, Italy, and other European nations, with organizers reporting high participation.
articles.description: Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez warned of a “very high risk” of disorder, especially after dark on Halloween

articles.headline: Oleshky evacuees reunite with families in northern Ukraine following ceasefire
articles.title: Emotional reunions with loved ones for Oleshky evacuees
articles.summary: Displaced residents from the occupied city of Oleshky met relatives at a designated site in the Chernihiv region after crossing the border from Belarus. The relocations followed a temporary truce brokered by United States First Lady Melania Trump that commenced across the Kherson frontline on Tuesday. Buses and ambulances transported the individuals who had previously journeyed through Crimea and Russia. The cessation of hostilities is scheduled to conclude on Sunday 1 November, according to BBC correspondent Dan Johnson reporting from the northern border.
articles.description: The BBC's Dan Johnson travelled to the northern Ukrainian border with Belarus after evacuated Oleshky residents arrived in buses and ambulances following a temporary ceasefire.

articles.headline: Police in Hyderabad rescue 43 women and arrest eight suspects in illegal egg harvesting racket
articles.title: 43 women rescued in illegal human egg harvesting racket in Hyderabad
articles.summary: Begumpet and Saroornagar police rescued 43 women and arrested eight suspects during simultaneous raids at four premises in Hyderabad. Authorities busted an alleged commercial egg harvesting racket that recruited women from various states by offering monetary incentives. Police seized documents, mobile phones, and medical supplies while investigating compliance under the Assisted Reproductive Technology Act.
articles.description: Police examine alleged recruitment of women across States, suspected use of rented premises and links with fertility centres and ART banks in Hyderabad

articles.headline: Pakistan Prime Minister orders accelerated federal development projects in Gilgit-Baltistan region
articles.title: Pakistan PM orders fast-tracking of development projects in Gilgit-Baltistan
articles.summary: Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif directed officials to accelerate ongoing federal development projects in Gilgit-Baltistan and ensure the timely release of funds during a meeting in Islamabad. The region is a key component of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor passing through territory claimed by India. Officials reviewed progress on hydropower, infrastructure, and solar energy projects during the session.
articles.description: The development assumes significance for India as Gilgit-Baltistan is illegally and forcibly occupied by Pakistan

articles.headline: United Nations political mission in Somalia concludes operations after three decades
articles.title: UN ends its Somalia political mission after three decades
articles.summary: The United Nations political mission in Somalia officially concluded operations after a two-year transition period, ending over three decades of peacebuilding efforts in the nation. Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud previously requested the termination of the mandate. The transition occurs as the government continues its fight against Al-Shabaab amid international funding cuts and upcoming elections scheduled for May.
articles.description: UNSOM was established by the UN Security Council in 2013 to support Somali authorities in the transition to democracy and the rule of law after more than two decades of conflict involving militias, Islamist groups and criminal gangs

articles.headline: Two students injured after classroom ceiling collapses in Khammam district
articles.title: Two students injured as concrete layer falls from classroom ceiling in State-run Gurukul in Khammam district
articles.summary: Two ninth-grade students sustained injuries when a concrete layer from their classroom ceiling fell on them while attending class at a State-run Gurukul in Bonakal mandal headquarters town. The victims received initial treatment at a local Primary Health Centre before being transferred to the Government General Hospital in Khammam. Both are currently reported to be out of danger, while student union leaders demand structural inspections.

articles.headline: Telangana government sets maximum retail prices for three fine rice varieties
articles.title: Telangana govt. announces maximum retail price of three fine rice varieties between ₹66 and ₹79 per kg
articles.summary: The Telangana government established price caps for high-demand fine rice varieties in Hyderabad and Medchal following discussions with wholesalers and retailers. The new maximum retail prices per kilogram are set at sixty-six rupees for BPT and KNM, seventy-four rupees for RNR and Telangana Sona, and seventy-nine rupees for HMT and JSR varieties. Officials warned that violations will face strict enforcement actions from the Civil Supplies department.

articles.headline: SEBI chairman says market regulator monitors governance developments at Tata Group
articles.title: SEBI chairman says market regulator keeping eye on Tata Group developments
articles.summary: Securities and Exchange Board of India Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey stated that the market regulator is actively observing governance developments involving the holding company level of the Tata Group. Speaking in Mumbai, Pandey emphasized that the conglomerate's twenty-six publicly listed companies and their promoters remain fully subject to standard disclosure and compliance regulations. The remarks followed ongoing discussions regarding governance matters and proposed listings at Tata Sons.
articles.description: The comments came amid differences over governance matters at Tata Sons

articles.headline: Thousands of protesters gather across German cities amid student demonstrations
articles.title: Thousands rally in Berlin as Gen Z protests in more than 30 German cities
articles.summary: Thousands of demonstrators assembled in Berlin and over thirty other German locations during a wave of nationwide student protests organized by the Gen Z Regelt alliance. Participants voiced strong opposition against government education funding cuts, rising living costs, and military spending. While most demonstrations remained calm, scuffles occurred in Cologne as police moved to contain a march during the coordinated events.
articles.description: Demonstrations sweeping Europe are inspiring young Germans frustrated by rising costs of living amid military spending.

articles.headline: Iran rules out bilateral meetings with United States despite rising tensions
articles.title: Iran has no plans for talks with U.S.: Foreign Minister
articles.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that Tehran has no ongoing plans for direct meetings with American officials despite growing concerns regarding a return to armed conflict. Speaking to Al Jazeera and cited by the state news agency IRNA, Araghchi confirmed that Iran received and reviewed a written message from United States Vice President J.D. Vance. He cautioned that Washington must avoid sowing discord while noting that diplomatic consultations continue through regional mediators.
articles.description: Araghchi confirmed that Iran received a letter from U.S. Vice President J. D. Vance, following days of diplomatic efforts to head off a return to violence

articles.headline: Enforcement Directorate detains Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan outside jail
articles.title: ED detains SP leader Azam Khan from outside Rampur jail as soon as he comes out on bail
